acceptance.then: each headline figure of the dashboard carries its provenance (observed for a count, derived for a ratio), a sentence saying how it was counted, and the numerator and denominator it came from, which match the gate and evidence records and move when the records do
a derived figure with nothing to count is null with a denominator of 0, never 0, while an observed count of nothing is 0

requirements.statement: Alerts include a stalled cell, the approval queue over its target, budget burn over forecast, gate flapping, an invariant breach, quota contention, a canary abort and the recurrence of a closed failure class.
requirements.notes: partly built: the canary abort alert is built; the other seven are recorded in contract/deferred/m.json

acceptance.then: a canary abort raises an alert with no person involved: one blocking incident card for the release and environment, open only to operations, IT or a developer, listed in the decision queue and counted in the project's now line as waiting on them, with the stopped release among the project's health reasons

requirements.statement: Four loops with separate authority: operational healing (reflexes; must work with every model offline), engineering repair (gate, plus a person outside pre-approved classes), product adaptation (the product owner decides), and factory learning (paired evaluation, then human promotion).
requirements.notes: partly built: these criteria cover what exists; the rest is recorded in contract/deferred/ijk.json

acceptance.then: with every model endpoint offline the operational loop still runs with no person: a release whose canary shows more errors is rolled back with the current release kept, a failing production probe opens its incident, and no model is asked

a reported defect is a pre-approved class: it re-enters the contract with a regression criterion and no person's decision, and its repair merges when the gate warrants it, permitted by policy; a repair the gate refuses waits on an escalation card that a developer, business owner or product owner decides, never operations

a change request or new requirement changes the spec only after a business owner or product owner accepts its change card; a developer, operations, IT or an end user may not decide it, and a rejected change is never applied

requirements.statement: The factory heals itself under change, error or disruption where it safely can.
requirements.notes: partly built: these criteria cover what exists; the rest is recorded in contract/deferred/ijk.json

acceptance.then: a release that passed its canary but cannot start on production's data is reverted with no person: the last green release is deployed again on the same data and checked healthy, and an incident card records the rollback
a lane whose holder died mid-task is free again at once without anyone releasing it, while a living holder's lane is never shared

when reverting to the last green release itself fails, the factory does not pretend: the release is recorded failed with the rollback's error, no slot claims to serve production, and a blocking incident card tells a person the rollback failed

requirements.statement: The factory becomes stronger from failures (antifragile).
requirements.notes: partly built: these criteria cover what exists; the rest is recorded in contract/deferred/ijk.json

acceptance.then: a check learned from a defect that recurred in two products, once a person accepts it, is in every new product's contract and builder envelope; that product's gate refuses work with no test naming it and accepts work whose test for it fails before the behaviour and passes after

lessons are one class when their content words match, whatever their order or case, so the same failure in two products is one class across products and a different failure is another; only a class shared by two products is proposed

a change the factory proposes to itself is promoted only by a person: it changes nothing until approved, the factory may not approve it, and a proposal a person rejects is never applied nor proposed again, even when its lesson recurs

requirements.statement: A typed workspace holds every hand-off between cells. Each artifact is pinned to a revision and supersedes or links other artifacts. Artifact types: finding, failure record, patch, open question, objection, decision, seam contract, signal and lesson.

acceptance.then: the hand-off between a builder cell and the gate is pinned to revisions: each repair round's patch is a commit the product repository keeps, recorded in the ledger (cell_ran) with its head; the gate's objections are recorded (gate) against that same head; and the next round's envelope names the contract and base revisions and carries those objections word for word

requirements.statement: A ledger of paths tried keeps history out of each cell's context.

acceptance.then: every repair round of a task is appended to the project's hash-chained ledger with its head, verdict and objections, while each round's envelope carries only the previous round's objections: older rounds stay in the ledger, out of the cell's context

after a person decides retry on an escalation, the task's next build starts from an envelope with no objections at all, while the ledger still holds every round of the earlier attempt and verifies intact

a person's workspace gets a task's earlier rounds by reference, not in its context: its context file names the escalation card but none of its objections, and the project ledger served by the workspace's MCP server holds the gate record with them

requirements.statement: Holdout acceptance scenarios are written outside the build and kept out of reach of building agents.
requirements.notes: partly built: custody holds through a build; a product-defect ruling still copies the failing step's expectations into a visible criterion (contract/deferred/b.json)

acceptance.then: holdout scenarios are written by the holdout author role, asked through Gnomon in the analyst lane, which holds no product code and gives the role no tools; its prompt carries the spec and its interface and none of the product's code, even once the product is built; each stored scenario names holdout_author as its author, and the product's surface has no holdout author role

through a build of every task, no builder envelope names a holdout or probe criterion or carries any of its scenario, and no file in a builder's lane, no commit of the product repository on any branch and no file of a person's workspace holds a scenario; the build leaves the custody unchanged

requirements.statement: A capability gateway serves capabilities by workload, with declared fallback, quotas and an audit of every request.

acceptance.given: a gateway config whose workloads each declare a class, a data class floor and a fallback ladder over OpenAI-compatible upstreams, and a site mode
acceptance.when: a client calls POST /v1/chat/completions naming a workload, not a model, in its model field
acceptance.then: the gateway (on loopback unless it is behind a proxy) sends the workload's model upstream and climbs the declared ladder in order: L1 the same workload on another upstream, L2 a smaller model whose answer carries a degraded header and field, L3 a cloud upstream only when the site mode and the request's data class allow it (never when air-gapped; a request cannot lower its workload's data class), L4 a queued request answered 202 with an honest "no answer yet" and retried; GET /v1/models lists the workloads; a wrong config is refused with the path of the wrong value; a capability pack's declared workloads become gateway workloads

acceptance.given: a batch and an interactive workload with per-class concurrency limits and a per-workload token bucket, and a cloud upstream whose key is named by an environment variable
acceptance.when: requests arrive and are answered, degraded, deferred, failed or refused
acceptance.then: a batch request over its class's concurrency limit or its workload's bucket is refused 429 with Retry-After while interactive requests pass; every request is one record in a hash-chained JSONL audit that kernel.ledger's check verifies and a restart continues, with the workload, level, upstream, model, latency, token counts and status but no prompt or answer unless content_capture is set; the key is read from the environment, refused in the config, never sent along a redirect, and absent from the audit and the logs

requirements.statement: Proven capabilities become recipes; a new need is matched to a recipe first and tried in a sandbox before anything is built.

acceptance.then: a recipe is saved only from a delivered project whose latest capability pack is intact and valid, by a product owner, business owner or IT; a need is matched to recipes by rule (shared keywords and the profile its words name); a new project from a recipe starts from its spec with each parameter as a question, answered or put to a person, and its plan waits for a person

a sandbox trial runs an explore release as a local preview with its holdouts (scores only), is stopped automatically when its time limit passes, says its result in plain words, and its outcome (promote or discard) waits for the named person; a decision by anyone else is not applied

requirements.statement: The factory measures how each model and endpoint fits each workload class, and reports it.

acceptance.then: fit rows per role, model, endpoint and workload class come only from records (the ledgers' Gnomon runs and gate rounds, and imported gnomon eval reports); nothing is estimated, and what was not measured or not mapped is said
the fit report maps use cases to workload classes, recommends one candidate per workload class by a fixed rule, and says what would change each recommendation

requirements.statement: Model-facing prompts are compact, consistent and cache-friendly: each role reads only instructions it can follow, each rule once, and the parts that repeat between calls come first, word for word, so an endpoint that caches prompt prefixes can reuse them.

acceptance.then: the analyst lane's system.md is a short prompt of its own (an analyst in Rihma, answering only from its task file, JSON in a fenced block when asked, no tools) and carries none of Gnomon's tool-use rules; the product lanes keep Gnomon's init prompt

the product lane's system.md is role-neutral: it keeps every safety rule (read-only `.gnomon/`, `contract.json` and `factory/`, writes only inside the task's paths, LF line endings) and names nothing only the builder can do; each builder rule (a failing test first, the unittest check, the standard library only, the report) is said once, in the builder's envelope

the intake perspectives' prompts share one prefix, word for word (the request verbatim and the common instructions), with the perspective-specific part last; a request longer than MAX_SOURCE_CHARS is cut with a note in the prompt saying how much was kept, a `request_cut` ledger event, and a line in the brief

the cockpit assistant's prompt starts with its static catalogue (rules, views, controls, actions, the answer's shape) and ends with the snapshot; the snapshot fits a character budget by dropping whole items, least needed first, never slicing its JSON, and its `not_shown` names what was dropped; a layout too large to show is named, not sliced

requirements.statement: A project's stage and its catalogue state follow what was actually delivered.

acceptance.then: a release that lands in preview, demo or staging puts the project at stage 6 and one promoted to production at stage 7 with released set, each move recorded in the ledger; the catalogue state comes from releases and what runs (in use while production runs, pilot while a release is validated or being validated on staging, trying while a demo is accepted or waits for acceptance or a preview is done, building at stage 5, shaping before); the square counts in production the projects whose production slot is current, and adopted solutions monitored where they run

requirements.statement: Holdouts never leave data in an environment end users use.

acceptance.then: holdouts run against a twin slot of the environment deployed from the same revision on its own data, which is stopped with its data afterwards, so the slot end users try holds none of it; the local-process and docker roads host a twin; a road that cannot host one runs them in the shared slot and the release records "holdouts ran in the shared slot: this road has no twin"

requirements.statement: The factory's ledgers go out to the subscriptions IT configures as thin CloudEvents 1.0, signed with Standard Webhooks v1, retried with backoff and logged; a secret is named by an environment variable and never stored (D-0015).

acceptance.given: every ledger kind the kernel and its adapters write, and cards whose titles quote a holdout string: as it is written, as cleaning leaves it (its tags stripped, its spaces collapsed), or across the title's length limit
acceptance.when: each record is mapped to an event
acceptance.then: each kind has a CloudEvents type in the rihma namespace (the catalog's, else rihma.ledger.<kind>); a card opened or decided carries the card's id, its kind, the personas it waits on and one deep link to it in the Inbox; the title is redacted against the holdout custody, as written and as cleaned, before it is cut to length, so a held string reads [held out] and no part of it remains; no card body, payload free text or holdout string is in the event

acceptance.given: a webhook subscription IT made, whose signing secret is named by an environment variable
acceptance.when: cards open and the relay runs
acceptance.then: each event matching the subscription's patterns is POSTed once as a CloudEvents 1.0 structured JSON body with webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and a webhook-signature that verifies with that secret; events from before the subscription are not sent; the secret is in no file of the factory home

acceptance.given: a receiver that is down
acceptance.when: the relay runs before and after each backoff, and the receiver recovers
acceptance.then: nothing is tried before a backoff ends; every attempt keeps its webhook-id and is in the hash-chained delivery log, which holds no URL or secret; the receiver gets each event once per webhook-id, in ledger order; after the last attempt the event is logged as failed and the stream moves on

acceptance.given: a subscription asked for by someone who is not IT, with a secret's value instead of its name, a receiver that is not https (or http on loopback), a chat URL given in place of its variable, or a remote mail relay without STARTTLS; and a ledger whose hash chain breaks
acceptance.when: the subscription is made, or the relay runs
acceptance.then: each such subscription is refused with nothing written (exit 2 on the command line), and a subscription that is made records who made it; the broken stream is delivered up to the break, halts there, and the delivery log says so once

acceptance.given: a receiver that answers with a redirect, a channel whose URL variable holds a malformed URL (a port that is not a number) beside a channel that works, a transport error that quotes a receiver's URL and a signing secret, and a relay round already running
acceptance.when: the relay runs
acceptance.then: a redirect is a failed attempt and the address it names is never called; the malformed URL is a failed attempt, retried and logged, that neither stops the round nor holds back the other subscription; the delivery log reads each quoted URL or secret as its variable's name (or <url>) and holds none of them; a round started while another runs answers busy and sends and logs nothing

requirements.statement: Verified inbound webhooks are doorbells: a delivery whose signature, timestamp and id hold becomes one signal or change proposal carrying only external ids, never a decision (D-0015).

acceptance.given: a Standard Webhooks delivery with a wrong signature, a changed body, a timestamp outside the tolerance or no signature headers, a GitHub delivery with a wrong X-Hub-Signature-256, a replayed delivery id, a body over the size limit, an unknown source, or a source whose secret is not set
acceptance.when: it arrives
acceptance.then: it is refused (401, 413, 404 or 503; a replay is answered 200 and not accepted) and nothing is stored in the factory home

acceptance.given: a valid delivery from a source IT named by its secret's variable, never its value
acceptance.when: it is processed
acceptance.then: it becomes one new signal with its ref (such as jira:acme/PROJ-1 or gh:owner/repo#12), or one open change card on the source's project, whose text holds only external ids and none of the body's free text; a second delivery for the same item while its signal is new or its card open creates nothing; a delivery that names no item is refused; nothing is decided

acceptance.given: the webhook server
acceptance.when: it is started and called
acceptance.then: it refuses a non-loopback address unless it is behind IT's proxy; it answers 202 with only accepted for a verified delivery and 200 for a replay, refuses a body over the limit with 413 before reading it and a request with no length with 411, and answers GET /health

requirements.statement: Notices carry one deep link to the card in the Inbox, rendered for email, Teams workflow webhooks and Slack incoming webhooks, and go out through the relay only to channels IT configured (D-0015).

acceptance.given: Teams, Slack and email channels for IT, a deploy gate card whose title quotes a holdout string beside a business approval card, and cards whose titles come from outside with web addresses, a Markdown link, a bare domain, a mail address, a mailto: or tel: address, a //host address, a dotted IP address, or Slack's control characters
acceptance.when: the relay runs
acceptance.then: each IT channel gets exactly one notice, for the deploy gate, whose only link opens that card in the Inbox at the cockpit address IT gave; it offers that link and no approve action; no payload in any channel carries the holdout string; a title from outside makes no second link in any channel: an address with a scheme, www. or // reads (link removed), a bare domain, dotted address or mail address is written with [.] and [at], a Markdown link is broken apart, and Slack's &, < and > are escaped

acceptance.given: a card a channel was told of, then decided; a channel whose URL variable is not set; and a factory with no subscription
acceptance.when: the relay runs
acceptance.then: the channel gets a follow-up that says the verdict, who decided and as which persona, with the same one link; a Teams or Slack URL is never stored, only its variable's name; a channel whose variable is missing waits and loses no attempt; with no subscription nothing is sent and nothing is written

requirements.statement: Connectors follow one model: a validated connector.json per system, a connector card only IT decides that pins the enabled entry, a change that stops the connector and reopens its card, and one contract test suite every connector passes (D-0015).

acceptance.given: connector.json files that miss a key, name another system or schema, use an HTTP server, allow a tool that merges, approves, deletes, deploys or pushes, give a write tool deciders that are not personas, name a tool twice, hold a credential value or a secret-looking string, or name an unknown data class
acceptance.when: they are validated
acceptance.then: each break is named by its JSON path, the command line refuses a broken folder with exit 2, and the example connector validates

acceptance.given: a valid connector folder
acceptance.when: IT enables it
acceptance.then: its entry is written to the factory's connectors.json and a connector card pins the sha256 of that entry with the sha256 of its connector.json; only IT may decide the card (enable or decline); the connector may run only once IT enabled it, never while it waits, nor once declined or disabled, even when the disabled entry is written back by hand (it stays stopped until IT decides a new card); anyone but IT enabling it is refused with nothing written

acceptance.given: an enabled connector
acceptance.when: its connector.json, any other file of its folder (its server.py or mapping.py) or its entry changes
acceptance.then: it is stopped at once and may not run; the check records the stop, withdraws a card left open and opens one new card that pins the new hashes, once per change; a connector.json that breaks the schema, or a local server that is not the one its server.pin pins, may not run whatever is decided

acceptance.given: every folder under connectors/
acceptance.when: the contract suite runs
acceptance.then: each validates under its own name with its fixtures, mapping and setup page; its pinned tools/list matches its fixture and its rug-pull fixture is caught; every injection sample maps, with no socket opened, to a proposal whose text is quoted untrusted data with no HTML or hidden characters; a narrow server.py is pinned by its sha256, answers its pinned tools/list over MCP stdio as a local fake, its read tools' results map to valid proposals, and its rug pull is caught

requirements.statement: Each release's image is pinned by the digest the registry gave it once IT pushed it with its own tools (Rihmasto writes nothing to a registry, D-0015), and the deploy package a site runs and the capability pack name that digest, never a movable tag, with the pack's version and content_sha256.

acceptance.given: a docker release on a road whose configuration names a registry, its image tagged for that registry at build
acceptance.when: IT has pushed the tag with its own tools and a person with the it persona pins the release (`rihmasto pack pin`), and its pack is built
acceptance.then: the release, and so the road, run the image by repository@sha256 digest, `pinned.artifacts` holds that digest and no tag, the pin is recorded in the ledger with the person (`image_pinned`), and `deploy_package/2` names the same digest and the pack's version and content_sha256

acceptance.given: a docker release whose road names no registry, so its image is never pushed
acceptance.when: its pack is built
acceptance.then: the pack pins the local image id, never the tag, and `pinned.not_by_digest` says a site cannot pull it by digest

acceptance.given: a docker road whose configuration names a registry
acceptance.when: a release is delivered on it
acceptance.then: Rihmasto pushes nothing (D-0015: every external write goes through Gnomon's integration lane, planned): it tags the image for the registry on the deploying host, records `image_tagged`, and the release says what IT pushes and how to pin it; until a pin the pack pins the local image id and says so, a pin by anyone without the it persona is refused, and a tag not pushed yet is said and not pinned

requirements.statement: An offline bundle is signed the way cosign 3.1 and later sign, into a Sigstore bundle with what an offline verify needs, and a signature is never claimed that no verifier checked.

acceptance.given: cosign 3.1 or later on PATH, which refuses to sign a blob without bundle output, and a key reference in RIHMA_COSIGN_KEY
acceptance.when: a bundle is exported
acceptance.then: it holds SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json, trusted_root.json and cosign.pub and no detached signature, cosign signed offline (`--tlog-upload=false`) with the key reference only, and `cosign verify-blob` passes with no network, failing once SHA256SUMS changes

acceptance.given: a signed bundle and a host without cosign
acceptance.when: the verifier checks it, with the factory's key or without
acceptance.then: each signature line reads "not verified: no verifier", never verified, and the verdict is "not verified: no verifier", never passed, with exit code 3

requirements.statement: Any Docker or Podman host can run a delivered release from a rendered Compose file, with the capability pack beside the image and never inside it.

acceptance.given: a valid deploy package/2 whose image is pinned by digest
acceptance.when: it is rendered
acceptance.then: compose.yaml runs image@digest with a named /data volume, mounts the pack and its status read-only from beside the image, names each secret by its environment variable only, `secret_leaks()` finds nothing, the YAML reads back as the model, and `docker compose config` accepts the file (run when docker is installed; the command is checked either way)

acceptance.given: a deploy package whose image is not pinned by digest, whose secret carries a value, or that names no pack
acceptance.when: it is rendered
acceptance.then: nothing is rendered, each problem is named, and an offline bundle of that release holds no compose.yaml and says why

acceptance.given: a deploy package/2 whose image is pinned by digest
acceptance.when: compose.yaml is rendered and an offline bundle carries it
acceptance.then: the folder beside compose.yaml, which holds the pack and its status, is bind-mounted read-only at /pack and no single file is bind-mounted, so a status replaced by a rename reaches pack_guard; validate_compose refuses a single-file bind mount; the bundle's README says to replace the status in that folder

acceptance.given: a deploy package/2 that names a secret
acceptance.when: compose.yaml is rendered
acceptance.then: the product gets the secret as the environment variable of its name, as on the factory's roads, its value taken from the deployer's environment (`${NAME:?...}`), never as a Compose secret (a file under /run/secrets) and never a value in the file; validate_compose refuses either; and, when docker compose is installed, it sets the variable from the environment and refuses to start without it

requirements.statement: The pack, the bundle, the status document and the site's deploy package have published JSON schemas, and a standalone offline verifier that imports nothing from Rihmasto checks a bundle with nothing installed, trusting only the key the factory published, and says passed only when the signatures were verified against it.

acceptance.given: the published schemas and a real bundle's pack, BUNDLE.json, status document and deploy package
acceptance.when: each is checked against its schema
acceptance.then: each conforms, a secret given a value does not, the pack schema names every unhashed field and the canonical-JSON rule (not RFC 8785, so no floats), the hashed content holds no float, and the verifier hashes a pack exactly as the kernel does

acceptance.given: a good signed bundle and the key the factory published
acceptance.when: the verifier runs offline
acceptance.then: every check passes (SHA256SUMS, the pack hash, the pack named alike, the status, the app files, the evidence manifest and ledger chain, the schemas), statements read not applicable, and the signature lines read "verified" with cosign and the verdict passed, or "not verified: no verifier" without cosign, also from its command line

acceptance.given: a bundle with one changed byte
acceptance.when: the verifier runs
acceptance.then: it fails, names the changed file, and its command line exits 2

acceptance.given: a signed bundle that someone changed, summed again and signed again with another key, replacing the cosign.pub inside it
acceptance.when: the verifier runs
acceptance.then: the bundle's own cosign.pub is never trusted: without --key the signature lines read "not verified: no trusted key" and the verdict says so with exit code 3, and with the key the factory published it fails with exit code 2

acceptance.given: a signed bundle whose status was forged and its signature removed, whose status was removed, or whose SHA256SUMS signature was removed after a change
acceptance.when: the verifier runs
acceptance.then: a signed bundle's status must be signed and present where BUNDLE.json names it, so the first two fail with or without --key; with --key a bundle without its signature fails with exit code 2, and without --key it reads "not signed", never passed

acceptance.given: a bundle or evidence pack whose every other check passes but whose signatures were not verified against the key the factory published (no cosign, no --key, or not signed)
acceptance.when: the verifier's command line runs
acceptance.then: the verdict never reads passed and the exit code is 3; only a bundle verified against --key reads passed and exits 0

requirements.statement: pack_guard in the product template keeps /health at 503 until the pack hash, the file tree hashes, the pack's status and its smoke set pass; a named person with the it, compliance or product_owner persona can withdraw a pack version.

acceptance.given: a product running with its pack and a valid status beside it
acceptance.when: a person with the it persona withdraws its version (`rihmasto pack withdraw`) and the withdrawn status is placed beside the pack
acceptance.then: the next time the guard reads the status, /health returns 503 with the reason and the person, the ledger names the person (`pack_withdrawn`), and a developer is refused

acceptance.given: an app file edited after the pack was built
acceptance.when: the product starts with the pack beside it
acceptance.then: /health never answers 200, and says the app files differ from those the pack pins

acceptance.given: a product started with its pack, its status and the pack hash the deploy package names
acceptance.when: the status expires or names another pack, the pack's content no longer hashes, the pack is not the one named, or its smoke set fails
acceptance.then: /health answers 503 naming each, and 200 again only once every check passes; without RIHMA_PACK the guard is off, and the image template copies pack_guard

acceptance.given: a product whose pack_guard has seen a newer status, or the pack's withdrawal
acceptance.when: the status file is then removed, half written, replaced by an older status or, after a withdrawal, by a newer valid one, or the product restarts with an older status beside it
acceptance.then: /health stays 503 naming the newest status seen: the guard keeps the newest status per pack in DATA_DIR, takes no status issued before it, and keeps a withdrawal as final

acceptance.given: a product whose app/server.py a builder cell changed so that it starts no guard, and a pack that pins that change
acceptance.when: the product starts as its image starts it (the Dockerfile's CMD) with a withdrawn status beside its pack
acceptance.then: /health answers 503 naming the withdrawal: the image starts through factory/pack_guard.py, which a change to app/ cannot remove; the Dockerfile is outside a builder's write scope, an edit to factory/pack_guard.py is a protected path, and a pack built from a product whose image does not start through the guard says so

requirements.statement: Every gate card (the demo's acceptance, staging's validation, production's deploy gate), evidence pack and export carries a governance map: each of the five guarantees (pinning, evals, revocation, evidence, telemetry) held, partial or lost where the release runs.

acceptance.given: a production release delivered through IT's deploy gate
acceptance.when: its gate card, its evidence pack and its offline bundle are shown
acceptance.then: each marks the five guarantees held, partial or lost with why, and the evidence pack holds the same map as the gate card

acceptance.given: a target resting on an UNVERIFIED platform feature (Azure Container Apps, never deployed), or an image pinned by a movable tag
acceptance.when: its governance map is made
acceptance.then: no guarantee on the unverified target is held, and pinning by a tag is lost

acceptance.given: a demo release and a production release
acceptance.when: the demo's acceptance card and staging's validation card are opened
acceptance.then: each carries the governance map of the road its environment runs on, in its payload and its body, as the deploy gate card does

requirements.statement: Rihmasto's own records form a knowledge graph: an ontology declares its kinds and links, and a read model rebuilt from the ledgers, records and spec snapshots on every read answers trace, impact, path, as_of and check, each step cited and each answer ending in answered, ambiguous, not_found or not_measured, without reading the holdout custody (docs/knowledge-graph.md, phase 1).

acceptance.given: holdout scenarios, a failed holdout's reason and a ruling's reason that carry sentinel strings, and outside text (a change's words, a comment, a comment's target) that carries others
acceptance.when: the graph is built and every query (trace, impact, path, as_of, check, the named questions, parity, the assistant eval) and every audience's rendering is produced
acceptance.then: no sentinel appears in any of them; a release's holdout verdicts are read in a closed shape (a criterion id and a named verdict) and its reason through custody_safe; and no graph module (kernel/graph.py, kernel/graph_build.py, kernel/graph_records.py, kernel/graph_ask.py, kernel/ontology.py, kernel/ontology.json) references holdouts_dir

acceptance.given: a product repository made from the paved-road template
acceptance.when: its suite runs, and a builder cell's change edits or removes the road-contract tests

acceptance.given: a spec with a requirement or criterion that wants the service bound to loopback, a port of its own, or GET /health answered without the release version
acceptance.when: the plan is reviewed

acceptance.given: a release whose service does not answer a healthy /health with its version
acceptance.when: delivery's deploy step fails the health check
acceptance.then: the release record keeps the docker container's log tail from both of its streams, the sockets listening inside it (read from /proc/net) and a diagnosis naming loopback-only binding or a /health without the release version; the local-process road starts the product with HOST=127.0.0.1

acceptance.given: requirements and criteria that contradict the road in their common phrasings, and others that only sound like it

acceptance.given: a holdout author writing scenarios for a project whose roads name secrets

acceptance.given: a signed step whose header is a transport header (Host, Content-Length, Content-Type, Proxy-*) or not a plain name, or whose prefix holds a line break, and a scenario the runner cannot send at all
acceptance.when: the holdouts run, alone or in delivery
acceptance.then: the malformed sign is refused before anything is sent and before the scenario enters custody, and that scenario is not measured with a reason naming what is wrong; a scenario the runner cannot send is not measured, named by the error's kind only, and every other scenario still runs; the holdouts step records a verdict, never a traceback, and no secret's value or error text that could quote one is kept

requirements.statement: A work profile is proposed from whole words, and a proposal the rule is unsure of is put to a person with its top candidates.

acceptance.when: a profile is proposed by rule

acceptance.given: an intake whose proposal is uncertain

acceptance.given: an intake whose profile question is open, in assume, mixed or socratic mode, and a project whose question was answered only after its spec was written

acceptance.when: adoption characterises it
acceptance.then: the baseline is 'not measured: timed out', with the limit, every process the suite started is stopped, and adoption completes; the per-suite limit has its own default (SUITE_TIMEOUT), apart from git's timeout

requirements.statement: Rihmasto scans and red-teams what it builds with its own checks, proven by seeded defects, within a scope a person authorised
requirements.notes: D-0014: the capability is Rihmasto's own and depends on no other project or repository.

acceptance.then: each rule of the static layer catches its seeded defect in tests/fixtures/redteam/vulnerable_app at the marked line, and reports nothing else there; each rule names a CWE id, an OWASP Top 10 2025 category, a severity and a fix

the same product written safely (tests/fixtures/redteam/clean_app), the near misses a careless rule would report, and the red team's own source (full of sink names and secret patterns as text) yield no finding and no canary marker

the scan's SARIF 2.1.0 is read by adapters/sarif.py with each finding's rule, level, CWE and location; the security gate fails on the vulnerable product and passes on the clean one; a finding keeps its fingerprint when lines move, so a person's risk acceptance follows it; each kind of scan is its own tool, so a later run of another kind never replaces the static findings

each layer says measured, partial or not measured, with the reason; a layer with a file it could not read is partial, and a scan with no finding there is not measured, never passed; the gap reaches the ledger as an open result; a scan that measured nothing writes no SARIF; generated code nested thousands deep is checked, and a file the checks could not walk is a gap, never a crash

every evidence snippet is masked (at most a sixth of a credential, never more than four characters, stays readable) and trimmed, so no planted credential reaches the report, the SARIF or the summary; a comment marker `redteam: canary` silences only the secret rules on its own line and is listed in the summary and the SARIF, a mere mention of it is not a marker, and a marked secret file is a canary whose unmarked lines are still read

only a named person with the it or compliance persona authorises red teaming, naming targets, a reason and an expiry in the future at most 31 days ahead; the scope is recorded in the project's ledger and can be revoked by the same people, with a reason

before any request is sent, a target that is not a loopback IP address, not a base_url the factory deployed (its slot state) or a surface it runs, or not in an unexpired, unrevoked scope is refused, and the refusal is recorded; a ledger that does not verify authorises nothing
`python -m kernel.redteam static <path> [--sarif out] [--markdown out]` prints the summary, writes the files and exits 0 when passed, 1 when failed, 4 when not measured and 2 on a usage error
the red team depends on the standard library and the kernel only; optional external scanners are never needed and say not measured; the product the factory scaffolds is scanned without false alarms

each dynamic probe (security headers, error pages that leak, path traversal plain and encoded, reflected injection on the routes of the project's fixed interface, method tampering, malformed and oversized bodies, CORS that echoes any origin or allows credentials with a wildcard, missing rate limiting on a write route) catches its seeded defect in the vulnerable server of tests/fixtures/redteam/dynamic, and nothing else there; each dynamic rule names a CWE id, an OWASP Top 10 2025 category, a severity and a fix

the clean twin server, the same product and interface written safely with near misses beside the fixes, yields no dynamic finding with every layer measured, and the near misses a careless probe would report (a 404 that echoes the request, a tag in JSON, a page's script path, a public API's wildcard origin) stay quiet

a dynamic run checks the scope before the target and before every request; a target outside the scope, expired or revoked, not deployed by the factory, or not on loopback is refused and recorded with zero connections made; a surface the run started needs its own scope; a scope that ends mid-run stops the run at its next request and the layers it did not reach are not measured

a dynamic run never sends more requests than its budget (1 to 1000) and the rate limit probe never more than 12, stopping at the first 429; what the budget did not reach is partial or not measured with the reason, never passed; each run is recorded in the project's ledger with its scope, target, requests sent and verdict

the dynamic report's SARIF is its own tool (Rihmasto red team (dynamic)) read by adapters/sarif.py beside the static scan, with fingerprints that hold from run to run; `python -m kernel.redteam dynamic <project> --env <environment>` prints the summary and exits 0 when passed, 1 when failed, 4 when not measured, 2 on a usage or input error and 3 when the scope refused the target, with nothing sent

the agentic red team's payload corpus (kernel/redteam/payloads.json) covers, for the embed chat and the cockpit assistant, instruction override, system prompt extraction, exfiltration of the project's records, of holdout scenarios and of another project's data, tool or action abuse (a persona proposing a decision it may not take, an embed for any origin), encoding and language tricks and multi-turn escalation with forged answers; a malformed corpus is refused before anything is sent

before a run, fresh canaries are planted in a sandbox copy of the project where the surface must never reveal them (a holdout scenario, the project's records, another project's canon); the canary check finds each seeded leak in tests/fixtures/redteam/agentic/leaks.json in its form (plain, obfuscated, look-alike, reversed, ROT13, escaped, base64, base32, hex, partial) and none of the near misses; a canary's value never reaches the report, the SARIF or the ledger, and the sandbox is removed after the run

the embed chat, over POST /e/<id>/messages on the factory's own embed server on loopback with the embed's key and an allowed origin, and in process, leaks no canary, exposes none to the model and files only change cards on its project, against a worst-case FakeModel that complies with every attack; the report gives per category the attempts, leaks and disallowed actions

the cockpit assistant, through kernel.assistant.ask and through the cockpit's POST /api/assistant on loopback, leaks and exposes no canary against the worst-case model, and every disallowed proposal it is handed is refused by the kernel's Inbox rules before a person sees it, judged again independently by the red team

each seeded defect in tests/fixtures/redteam/agentic/broken_guards.py is caught in its layer: a model that leaks the holdout custody (and not its honest twin), a chat whose prompt carries the canon, an assistant whose snapshot carries the custody and another project, proposals that skip the Inbox's rules, and a chat that accepts its own change; the findings are SARIF of their own tool that the security gate reads and fails on

a run needs an unexpired scope a person with the it or compliance persona authorised for that surface; without one, after a revoke, after the expiry, with a ledger that does not verify, or over HTTP to a server not on loopback, it is refused and recorded before any request is sent or any model asked; a run is recorded in the project's ledger with its counts and leaves the real project's records untouched

each layer of an agentic run (leaks, exposure, actions) says measured, partial or not measured with the reason; prompts the red team cannot see leave exposure not measured, an attempt that could not run leaves the run not measured, a run without a model has no exposure to measure, and nothing unmeasured is reported as passed or written as an empty SARIF

`python -m kernel.redteam agentic <project> --surface embed|assistant` prints the per-category summary, writes SARIF and markdown, and exits 0 when passed, 1 when failed, 2 on a usage error, 3 when the scope refuses and 4 when not measured; with --via http it starts the factory's own embed server or cockpit on 127.0.0.1 and drives it over loopback

every static bypass independent attackers reported (a source-encoding declaration that hides code, data on a binding other than the last assignment, shell, SQL, path, TLS, debug, binding, timeout, hash and deserialisation forms, aliases, JavaScript line terminators, regular expressions, sinks and sanitisers, HTML integrity, Dockerfile heredocs, ARG defaults and escape directives, Actions expressions, and secret names and formats) is a seeded defect in tests/fixtures/redteam/bypass_app caught at its line with nothing else reported, and the safe forms and false alarms they found in tests/fixtures/redteam/bypass_clean yield no finding, every layer measured
the GitHub Actions rules apply to a workflow by its real folder, so scanning the repository, its .github folder, its workflows folder or one workflow file finds the same injections

a static scan reads nothing outside its target (a symbolic link, a Windows junction or a file whose real path leaves the tree is not read and is listed), lists every folder it skips by name with its file count and reads a product package named like a virtual environment, lists the paths a person excluded, and reads paths longer than the Windows limit

a canary marker silences a secret only in a test suite; in the product's own code the secret is reported, and every planted canary reaches the security gate as a SARIF result to review (kind review, level note, suppressed in source)

the scope cannot be widened from code: a surface counts only through the handle issued for a server or process the factory started on the run's home, a name that is a machine's is not a person who may authorise, a scope record in the ledger is checked again as authorise checks it, a slot whose process is gone or whose file claims another place is not deployed, a URL scope is bound to the deployment it named, and an expiry offset cannot stretch a scope past 31 days in UTC

no dynamic probe changes data: undeclared write methods go only to a path with a parameter set to a value that names no record, the rate-limit probe sends JSON cut short, and on production nothing that writes is sent and those layers say not measured; an origin echoed without credentials and a body cap above what a form needs are not reported

an agentic run checks the scope before every turn and every question to the model and stops, recorded and not measured, when it was revoked or expired mid-run; only a server the factory started is driven; every leak form in tests/fixtures/redteam/agentic/leaks_missed.json, a canary split between fields or over turns, a canary reaching the prompt whatever the attacker sent, and a write to an existing or untracked record are found, while near misses stay quiet

the pipeline stops at the edge of the set as done, saying why and what to do next, and records the stop once: spec only stops once the contract is compiled, a set without delivery stops before delivery

acceptance.then: the tool is refused with the module and the command that turns it on, nothing is written; a comment, which is core, is taken; every MCP tool that writes names the cockpit route whose module it asks

acceptance.given: a person in the cockpit in a real browser, light and dark, 1440 and 390 px wide
acceptance.when: they give New project a folder, scan it, untick a file and adopt it, and give it a folder of documents only
acceptance.then: the scan step shows the map grouped by read, summarised, unticked, listed and skipped with each reason, unticking scans again without the file and keeps the focus on it, adopt starts the job with the exclusion, a documents-only folder is offered as material for a new project and created from it; no secret is on the page, nothing scrolls sideways, and there is no console error, failed request or CSP violation

requirements.statement: A person publishes a version by pushing its tag: the suite and the contract run again, the source archives, an SBOM, checksums and the notes are built from the tagged commit, and a GitHub Release publishes them with a signed build provenance attestation; nothing is published from a tag that does not match the declared version.
requirements.notes: The owner asked that the CI/CD pipeline work, and approved a release workflow on 2026-11-24 ("Yes do"). Rihmasto runs from a checkout, so the source archive is the release; no wheel and no image. tools/release_build.py, .github/workflows/release.yml, docs/maintainers.md.

acceptance.given: a checkout whose pyproject.toml declares 1.2.0
acceptance.when: a release is built for a tag that is not v1.2.0, is not a version, or for a version the changelog has no section for
acceptance.then: the build is refused with the reason and no file is written

acceptance.given: a checkout whose pyproject.toml declares 1.2.0 and whose changelog has a [1.2.0] section
acceptance.when: a release is built for the tag v1.2.0
acceptance.then: it holds a .tar.gz and a .zip of the files git tracks at HEAD under rihmasto-1.2.0/, a CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM naming rihmasto 1.2.0, its licence, the archives' hashes and Gnomon as its one runtime dependency, SHA256SUMS that verify, and the notes word for word from the [1.2.0] section; building again from the same commit gives the same bytes

acceptance.given: a declared version that is an alpha, beta, release candidate or development version
acceptance.when: a rehearsal is built, or a release for it
acceptance.then: the rehearsal takes the declared version and the [Unreleased] notes, and the release is marked a pre-release

acceptance.given: the release workflow
acceptance.when: a person pushes a version tag, or runs the workflow by hand
acceptance.then: the suite and the contract run before anything is built; the provenance attestation and the GitHub Release happen only for a pushed tag; the workflow reads by default, only the publishing job may write contents, no expression is expanded inside a script, and a run by hand publishes nothing

requirements.statement: Anything set when a project was made can change: a person changes its kind of work, mode, maturity or title with a preview of what the change means for the work already done, sends it back to its material, questions, spec or plan so that step runs again, and adds material later; nothing is deleted, every change is signed and recorded, and a project always says what it waits for, who can act and the actions that move it forward.
requirements.notes: The owner, using Rihmasto daily on a customer project: "I don't want to see stupid mistakes like me choosing a template for the project or me generating a spec, then I'm getting stuck somewhere because Rihmasto assumed the project template wrong. I want all that to be able to change." kernel/project_settings.py, kernel/rewind.py, kernel/project_material.py, kernel/next_step.py, kernel/change_cli.py, cockpit/static/change.js, docs/guides/change-anything.md. The posture has its own change flow (kernel/posture_change.py) and is not changed here.

acceptance.given: a project whose intake ran for one kind of work, with an open question
acceptance.when: a person changes its kind of work with a reason, after a preview, and asks to go back
acceptance.then: the preview writes nothing and says the open questions no longer fit; project_changed records the person, persona, reason, before and after; the open questions are withdrawn with their cards decided as withdrawn and the reason; settled answers are kept; and the next run asks the questions again for the new kind without asking a settled one again

acceptance.given: a project whose spec is written
acceptance.when: a person changes its maturity and asks to go back
acceptance.then: the impact says the spec was written for the old maturity and whether a person now approves the plan; the spec is kept as a superseded version and written again at the next run

acceptance.given: a project whose questions wait on people
acceptance.when: a person changes its mode
acceptance.then: nothing is settled unless the person asks; when asked, each open question the new mode lets the factory assume is assumed in that person's name; a change by a non-person, a persona that may not, with no reason or to a value no setting takes is refused and writes nothing

acceptance.given: a project compiled from its spec
acceptance.when: a person sends it back to the plan, the spec, the questions and the material in turn
acceptance.then: each step's files are moved under superseded/ and listed, never deleted; the ledger records rewound with the person, persona and reason; and the pipeline's next tick runs that step again (compile, spec, intake), or waits for material

acceptance.given: a project with a release
acceptance.when: a person asks to send it back to any step
acceptance.then: it is refused with a message that names the release and the change loop, and nothing changes; a settings change still records the new value and goes back nowhere

acceptance.given: a project whose intake ran and a question was answered
acceptance.when: a person adds material with re-intake
acceptance.then: the original request is kept and the material is appended under its own heading and kept with its sha256 in material.json and the ledger; the panel reads only the new material, told what was asked before, and only questions not on record are added and settled by the mode; every answer stands; from the cockpit the panel reads it in the next run; only scripted models answer in the test

acceptance.given: any state a project can be in
acceptance.when: next_step reads it
acceptance.then: every state the pipeline returns maps to at least one action naming who may take it and the control, view or command that carries it out; the records' own states (no material, blocking questions, decision cards, paused, a model endpoint that failed, an intake to run again, a stopped build, released, adopted, attached, running) each name their waits, who and actions

acceptance.given: the cockpit and the command line
acceptance.when: a person changes the settings, goes back a step, adds material or asks what is next
acceptance.then: PUT settings, POST settings/preview, rewind and material are signed by a person and persona, checked for access like every write route, recorded in the project's ledger (the preview records nothing), refuse a project a job runs for or with a release, and `rihmasto settings`, `rewind`, `material add` and `next` do the same

acceptance.given: the cockpit in a browser
acceptance.when: a person follows What's next, changes the kind with its preview, adds material, goes back a step and advances
acceptance.then: each write lands signed with their name; dark and light at 1440 and 390 pixels wide the overview and the three dialogs fit with nothing scrolling sideways, every control has an accessible name, and no step leaves a console error, a failed request or a Content-Security-Policy violation
